title: HappyHorse Videos API
description: Generate or edit HappyHorse videos from text, first frames, multiple reference images, or video, with synchronous, asynchronous, and callback delivery.

async.description: When set to true, the interface immediately returns task_id, which can then be used to query the results through the Tasks API.

model.description: HappyHorse model name. Different actions only support the corresponding model family.

ratio.description: Output video aspect ratio. Text-to-video and reference image-to-video support this parameter; the first frame image-to-video will follow the aspect ratio of the first frame image.

action.description: Operation types. `generate` is for generating video from text, `image_to_video` is for generating video from the first frame image, `reference_to_video` is for generating video from reference images, and `video_edit` is for video editing based on video and reference images.

prompt.example: A cinematic white horse lifts its head, the mane moves gently in the sunrise wind, slow camera push in, warm film lighting
prompt.description: Text prompt words. Text-to-video, reference image to video, and video editing scenarios are required.

duration.description: Output video duration (seconds), value range 3–15. The output duration of `video_edit` is determined by the input video.

image_url.description: The input image URL for the first frame of the video. Only used by `image_to_video`.

video_url.description: URL of the video to be edited. For `video_edit` use only.

watermark.description: Whether to add the HappyHorse watermark. Default is off.

image_urls.description: Reference image URL array. `reference_to_video` supports 1–9 images, `video_edit` supports 0–5 images.

callback_url.description: Asynchronous callback address. After setting, the interface will immediately return task_id, and after the task is completed, the result will be POSTed to this address.

audio_setting.description: Audio strategy for video editing. `auto` is determined by the model, `origin` retains the original audio of the input video.

parameters.description: Specify the response format returned by the server. `application/x-ndjson` can be used for streaming progress responses.

title: Kling Motion Generation API
description: Kling motion-control video generation API. Generates controllable-motion video clips from a reference image and motion trajectory (motion brush, etc.), suitable for animated demos, character motion, and creative ads.

mode.description: Video generation mode, optional, enumeration values: `std` (standard mode, 720p, lower consumption) or `pro` (professional mode, 1080p, higher image quality). The default value is `std`.

async.description: Whether to process in asynchronous mode. When set to `true`, the interface immediately returns `task_id`, without the need to provide `callback_url`, and then the result can be obtained by polling the corresponding task query interface; if `callback_url` is also provided, the result will be pushed to that callback address.

prompt.example: White ceramic coffee mug on glossy marble countertop with morning window light. Camera slowly rotates 360 degrees around the mug, pausing briefly at the handle.
prompt.description: Text prompts can contain both positive and negative descriptions simultaneously.

image_url.description: Character appearance reference image URL. Supports JPG/JPEG/PNG, file ≤50MB, both width and height ≥300px, aspect ratio 1:2.5–2.5:1; the character should clearly show the upper body or full body and head, avoiding obstruction, upside-down, lying down, or an overly small subject.

video_url.description: Motion reference video URL. Supports MP4/MOV, file ≤100MB, width and height each 340–3850px, at least 3 seconds; when `character_orientation=image`, maximum 10 seconds, when `character_orientation=video`, maximum 30 seconds. It is recommended to use a continuous single-shot video in which the person remains in the frame at all times.

model_name.description: Model name, optional, enumeration values: `kling-v2-6` or `kling-v3`. If not provided, the server's default model will be used.

callback_url.description: Callback URL, after the video generation is complete, the system will send a callback notification to this URL.

watermark_info.description: Watermark configuration, optional. The object format is `{ "enabled": true }`. When `enabled` is set to `true`, results with watermarks are generated additionally, and custom watermarks are not supported at this time.

keep_original_sound.description: Whether to keep the original audio of the reference video, optional, enumeration values: `yes` (keep) or `no` (remove). The default value is `yes`.

character_orientation.description: Generate the orientation of characters in the video, which can be chosen to be consistent with the reference image (`image`) or reference video (`video`).

title: OpenAI Images Generations API
description: Unified image generation endpoint compatible with the OpenAI Images API. A single endpoint supports DALL·E 2/3, the full GPT Image family (gpt-image-1, gpt-image-1.5, gpt-image-2), and Google's Nano Banana family (nano-banana, nano-banana-2, nano-banana-pro). Fine-grained control via size, quality, style, background, output_format, moderation, etc., with transparent background, PNG/JPEG/WebP outputs, and optional callback_url for async delivery.

n.description: The number of images to generate, ranging from 1 to 10. `dall-e-3` is fixed at `1`. The `dall-e-2`, `gpt-image-1` / `gpt-image-1.5` / `gpt-image-2` / `gpt-image-2.5-flare` / `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` series, as well as the `nano-banana` / `nano-banana-2-lite` / `nano-banana-2` / `nano-banana-2.1` / `nano-banana-pro` series all support `n>1`: the default model and `:reverse` are billed by the number of successfully generated images, while `:official` is charged based on the actual Token usage aggregated across the entire response, and will not be multiplied repeatedly by `n`. Note that `response_format=b64_json` only supports `n=1`; when `n>1`, please use the default URL return. If some images fail to generate, only the successfully generated ones will be returned and billed.

size.description: Image size, in the format `widthxheight`, or enter `auto` to select the aspect ratio based on the prompt semantics. **The GPT Image 2 series (`gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`)** accepts any properly formatted `WIDTHxHEIGHT` value, including 1K presets (`1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, `1024x1536`, `1792x1024`, `1024x1792`), 2K presets (`2048x2048`, `2048x1536`, `1536x2048`, `2048x1152`, `1152x2048`), 4K presets (`2880x2880`, `3264x2448`, `2448x3264`, `3840x2160`, `2160x3840`), as well as any custom size; the default model and `:reverse` are billed per image, while the size and quality of `:official` affect Token usage and are billed based on actual usage. Size limits: custom dimensions must be multiples of 16, the longer side must not exceed 3840, the total pixel count must be 655,360–8,294,400, and the aspect ratio must not exceed 3:1. `dall-e-2` supports: `256x256`, `512x512`, `1024x1024`. `dall-e-3` supports: `1024x1024`, `1792x1024`, `1024x1792`. When `auto` is explicitly passed, the platform determines the result in a continuous aspect-ratio space in the following order: explicit pixels or ratios, named standards (paper / print materials / platform placements / advertisements / devices / photography / film), medium conventions, and composition. In addition to common ratios, non-preset ratios such as `1.91:1`, `1.85:1`, `2.39:1`, and ISO paper `1:√2` can also be retained; the result will be normalized to multiples of 16 and the pixel budget supported by the service. When automatic determination is unavailable, it falls back to the model's default aspect ratio. Omitting the `size` field directly uses the model's default aspect ratio. If you have strict pixel requirements, please directly pass `WIDTHxHEIGHT`.

async.description: Whether to process in asynchronous mode. When set to `true`, the interface immediately returns `task_id`, without the need to provide `callback_url`, and then the result can be obtained by polling the corresponding task query interface; if `callback_url` is also provided, the result will be pushed to that callback address.

model.description: Models for image generation. Supports OpenAI's `dall-e-2`, `dall-e-3`, `gpt-image-1` / `gpt-image-1.5` / `gpt-image-2` / `gpt-image-2.5-flare` / `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` series, as well as Google's `nano-banana` / `nano-banana-2-lite` / `nano-banana-2` / `nano-banana-2.1` / `nano-banana-pro`. Different models vary in their support for the `size`, `quality`, `style`, `background`, `output_format`, `moderation`, and `response_format` parameters; see the description of each field for details. `gpt-image-2` provides `gpt-image-2:official` (official channel, stable and compliant, billed based on the actual Token usage of text input and image output) and `gpt-image-2:reverse` (equivalent to the default `gpt-image-2`, with better cost-effectiveness); `gpt-image-2.5-flare` and `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` also each provide same-named `:official` variants, billed based on actual Token usage.

moderation.description: The content review levels of the GPT image model. `low` will relax the filtering strength; `auto` uses the default policy.

callback_url.description: Optional callback URL. Once provided, the API will immediately return `task_id` and will push the results to that URL via a POST request after the image generation is complete. The callback payload contains `task_id`, `trace_id`, `success` (boolean), and the complete response data or error information.

partial_images.description: The number of intermediate images sent during the streaming process (0-3). `0` indicates that the final image is returned directly in one event.

response_format.description: Return format: `url` (default) or `b64_json`. When using `url`, the platform will convert results that only return base64 into accessible CDN URLs; when explicitly using `b64_json`, the base64 content is retained. `b64_json` only supports `n=1`.

title: Suno Audios Generation API
description: Suno AI music generation API, generates 2 songs per request with extension support.

bpm.description: Sound effect target speed (beats per minute), optional only when `action` is `sounds`, must be an integer from 1 to 300.

key.description: The target mood of the sound effect, optional only when `action` is `sounds`.

async.description: Whether to process in asynchronous mode. When set to `true`, the interface immediately returns `task_id`, without the need to provide `callback_url`, and then the result can be obtained by polling the corresponding task query interface; if `callback_url` is also provided, the result will be pushed to that callback address.

lyric.description: Lyrics for generating music under custom mode (`custom` is `true`). `chirp-v3-5` and `chirp-v4` have a maximum of 3000 characters; `chirp-v4-5` and above (including `chirp-v5`, `chirp-v5-5`) have a maximum of 5000 characters.

model.description: Models used to generate music. Supports `chirp-v6`, `chirp-v6-wild`, and `chirp-v6-mini`; `chirp-v6` is recommended. Legacy model names remain compatible.

sound.description: The sound effect description to be generated, required when `action` is `sounds`.

style.description: Music style description. `chirp-v3-5` and `chirp-v4` support a maximum of 200 characters; `chirp-v4-5` and above (including `chirp-v5`, `chirp-v5-5`) support a maximum of 1000 characters. Optional when `action` is `add_stem`.

title.description: Music title (custom mode). `chirp-v3-5`, `chirp-v4` support up to 80 characters; `chirp-v4-5` and above (including `chirp-v5`, `chirp-v5-5`) support up to 100 characters. Optional when `action` is `add_stem`; required when `action` is `adjust_speed`.

action.description: Music generation operation types. `generate`: generate audio based on a prompt; `extend`: continue generating based on existing audio; `concat`: stitch existing audio clips into a complete track; `cover`: replicate the musical style of an existing track and reinterpret it; `upload_cover`: create a style cover of uploaded audio; `upload_extend`: extend and continue generating uploaded audio; `artist_consistency`: sing a new song in the style of a specified singer (Persona); `artist_consistency_vox`: sing a new song in the style of a specified singer using VOX mode; `stems`: separate a song into vocal and instrumental tracks; `all_stems`: separate a song into all individual tracks (vocals, drums, bass, other instruments); `add_stem`: add a new track to existing audio, with required `audio_id` and `stem_type`, and optional `prompt`, `title`, and `style`; `extract_stem`: extract a specified track from existing audio, with required `audio_id` and `stem_type`, and optional `audio_format`; `sounds`: generate standalone sound effects, with required `sound` and `sound_type`, and optional `bpm` and `key`; `adjust_speed`: adjust the playback speed of existing audio, with required `audio_id`, `speed_multiplier`, and `title`, while `keep_pitch` is optional; `replace_section`: replace a clip within a specified time range; `underpainting`: generate and add AI accompaniment for an uploaded vocal track; `overpainting`: generate and add AI vocals for an uploaded accompaniment track; `samples`: select a start and end range from an existing audio clip for sample-based creation; `remaster`: remaster existing audio to improve sound quality; `mashup`: mix and stitch multiple songs into one track; `inspo`: Inspo inspiration creation feature, using 1 to 4 dragged or uploaded reference audio clips to inspire entirely new music creation.

custom.description: Whether to enable the custom mode flag. If `true`, the audio will be generated based on the lyrics; otherwise, it will be generated based on the prompts.

prompt.description: Prompt words used to generate music in inspiration mode (effective when `custom` is `false`), with a maximum length of 500 characters. For custom mode, use `lyric` and `style` instead. When `action` is `add_stem`, this field is optional and is used to describe the track to be added.

variety.description: The diversity strength of the generated results, optional: `off`, `normal`, `high`, `extra`, `max`. Only `generate` and `add_stem` are supported; passing it to other actions will return 400.

audio_id.description: ID of the existing audio. This field is required when `action` is `extend`, `concat`, `add_stem`, `extract_stem`, or `adjust_speed`.

duration.description: Desired song duration (seconds), must be an integer between 10 and 360. The platform will pass this value; specific operations, modes, or models may weaken or ignore it. This is a generation target rather than a strict final length; the actual duration is subject to the response.

max_mode.description: Whether to enable enhanced generation mode. Only `generate` (which also requires `custom` to be `true`) and `add_stem` are supported. When enabled, 1.12 and 1.344 Credits are consumed respectively; when disabled or omitted, billing is based on normal mode. Passing this parameter for other actions will return 400.

stem_type.description: Track type. Required when `action` is `add_stem` or `extract_stem`; supports `vocals`, `backing_vocals`, `drums`, `bass`, `guitar`, `keyboard`, `percussion`, `strings`, `synth`, `fx`, `brass`, `woodwinds`.

weirdness.description: Weirdness, ranges from 0 to 1. Higher values generally make the result more experimental; 0 will be passed as a valid value. The specific effect depends on the operation type, mode, and model.

audio_urls.description: List of reference audio URLs for the Inspo inspiration creation feature. You need to provide 1 to 4 publicly accessible HTTP(S) audio URLs. This field is required when `action` is `inspo`.

keep_pitch.description: Whether to maintain the original pitch when adjusting speed, defaults to `false`, only used for `adjust_speed`.

persona_id.description: Generate the singer Persona ID used when creating songs based on the unique style characteristics of the specified singer.

sound_type.description: Sound effect type, required when `action` is `sounds`. `one-shot` indicates a one-shot sound effect, and `loop` indicates a loopable sound effect.

continue_at.description: Continuation boundary, in seconds. For example, 213.5 indicates starting to generate subsequent segments from 3 minutes and 33.5 seconds. `lyric` and `style` only guide new content after this boundary and will not replace the lyrics or singing before the boundary in the source audio; if you want the entire song to use new lyrics, please use `generate` to regenerate it, or use `cover` to reinterpret it.

samples_end.description: Add the end time of the sample for the uploaded audio, which must be less than the total duration of the song.

audio_format.description: Output audio format, optional only when `action` is `extract_stem` or `sounds`, currently supports `mp3`.

audio_weight.description: Influence weight of audio or voice characteristics, ranging from 0 to 1; 0 is also a valid value. It can be used for operations such as generation, continuation, cover singing, adding audio tracks, and voice consistency; in scenarios without reference audio or voice characteristics, the model may weaken or ignore this value.

callback_url.description: Callback URL to be called after audio generation is complete.

instrumental.description: Pure accompaniment mode (no lyrics), default is `false`. When set to `true`, the lyrics filled in above will be ignored.

lyric_prompt.description: Prompts for automatically generating lyrics, effective only when `custom` is `true` and `lyric` is empty.

vocal_gender.description: Voice gender preference, optional `m` (male voice) or `f` (female voice). This is a generation preference and is not guaranteed to be strictly followed.

negative_tags.description: Styles or genre descriptions that are not desired to appear in the generated music, effective only in custom mode (`custom` is `true`). This API currently does not set a fixed character limit for this field; excessively long content may still be unable to be processed, so it is recommended to keep the description concise.

samples_start.description: Add a default start time for the uploaded audio sample, with a default value of 0.

style_influence.description: Style influence, range 0 to 1. Higher values generally make the result closer to `style`; 0 is passed as a valid value. The specific effect depends on the operation type, mode, and model.

mashup_audio_ids.description: Audio ID list for mixing and mashup. This field is required when `action` is `mashup`.

overpainting_end.description: Add the end time of the AI voice to the uploaded audio, which must be less than the total duration of the song.

speed_multiplier.description: Playback speed multiplier, required when `action` is `adjust_speed`, ranging from 0.25 to 4.

underpainting_end.description: Add the end time for the AI accompaniment to the uploaded audio, which must be less than the total duration of the song.

overpainting_start.description: Set the default start time for the AI voice of the uploaded audio to 0.

variation_category.description: Remaster variation intensity, only used for `remaster`, optional values are `high`, `normal`, `subtle`.

replace_section_end.description: When `action` is `replace_section`, specify the end time (in seconds) of the segment to be replaced.

underpainting_start.description: Set the default start time for the AI accompaniment added to the uploaded audio, with a default value of 0.

replace_section_start.description: When `action` is `replace_section`, specify the start time (in seconds) of the segment to be replaced.

replace_section_result_mode.description: When `action` is `replace_section`, specify the return format. `full_song` (default) will concatenate 2 candidates separately and return 2 complete songs; `candidates` will return 2 uncombined replacement segment candidates, which need to be selected before calling `concat`.

parameters.description: Specify the format of the response returned by the server. If not specified, the default format is `application/json`; if `application/x-ndjson` is specified, the response will be returned in a JSON format separated by newline characters, streamed back in chunks.

title: Kling Tasks API

description: OpenAI image editing API, input images and instructions, output modified images.

n.description: Number of images to generate (1-10). `dall-e-3` is fixed at `1`. The `dall-e-2`, `gpt-image-1` / `gpt-image-1.5` / `gpt-image-2` / `gpt-image-2.5-flare` / `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` series, as well as the `nano-banana` / `nano-banana-2-lite` / `nano-banana-2` / `nano-banana-2.1` / `nano-banana-pro` series all support `n>1`: the default model and `:reverse` are billed based on the number of successfully generated images, while `:official` is charged based on the actual Token usage aggregated across the entire response, without being multiplied repeatedly by `n`. Note that `response_format=b64_json` only supports `n=1`; when `n>1`, please use the default URL return. If some images fail to generate, only the successful ones will be returned and billed.

size.description: Image dimensions, in the format `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, or `auto`. **The GPT Image 2 series (`gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`)** accepts any `WIDTHxHEIGHT` value that conforms to this format, including 1K presets (`1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, `1024x1536`, `1792x1024`, `1024x1792`), 2K presets (`2048x2048`, `2048x1536`, `1536x2048`, `2048x1152`, `1152x2048`), 4K presets (`2880x2880`, `3264x2448`, `2448x3264`, `3840x2160`, `2160x3840`), and custom dimensions; the default model and `:reverse` are billed per image, while only the dimensions and quality of `:official` affect Token usage and are billed based on actual usage. Dimension limits: custom dimensions must be multiples of 16, the long side must be ≤ 3840, the total pixel count must be 655,360–8,294,400, and the aspect ratio must not exceed 3:1. `dall-e-2` supports: `256x256`, `512x512`, `1024x1024`. Omitting the `size` field is completely equivalent to explicitly passing `auto`: the GPT Image 2 series first identifies explicit pixels, ratios, landscape/portrait orientation, resolution tiers (such as 4K / high-res), or named canvases from the prompt; when a size intention is identified, it uses the planned specific dimensions, and when the prompt has no size requirement or automatic determination is unavailable, it falls back to the dimensions of the first reference image. The final dimensions will be normalized to the above limits; when absolute control is needed, please directly pass `WIDTHxHEIGHT`.

async.description: Whether to process in asynchronous mode. When set to `true`, the interface immediately returns `task_id`, without the need to provide `callback_url`, and then the result can be obtained by polling the corresponding task query interface; if `callback_url` is also provided, the result will be pushed to that callback address.

title: Kling Videos Generation API
description: Kuaishou Kling AI video generation API. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and start/end frame control across kling-v1, kling-v1-6, kling-v2-master, kling-v2-1-master, kling-v2-5-turbo, kling-v2-6, kling-v3, kling-v3-omni, and kling-video-o1, with standard/high-quality modes and multiple duration options.

mode.description: Video generation mode, optional. Supported values: `std` (high performance mode), `pro` (high quality mode), `4k` (native 4K, only supported by `kling-v3` and `kling-v3-omni`, incompatible with "motion control"). The default value is `std`.

async.description: Whether to process in asynchronous mode. When set to `true`, the interface immediately returns `task_id`, without the need to provide `callback_url`, and then the result can be obtained by polling the corresponding task query interface; if `callback_url` is also provided, the result will be pushed to that callback address.

model.description: The model used for generating videos, with a default value of kling-v1.

action.description: Video generation action. If the value is `text2video`, then generate a video based on the prompt.

prompt.example: White ceramic coffee mug on glossy marble countertop with morning window light. Camera slowly rotates 360 degrees around the mug, pausing briefly at the handle.
prompt.description: Prompts for generating videos. When using Omni All-Purpose Reference (model `kling-o1` or `kling-v3-omni`), you need to reference the corresponding numbers (starting from 1) in `image_list` / `video_list` in the form of `<<<image_1>>>`, `<<<video_1>>>` in the prompts for the model to apply these references; for example, "Change `<<<video_1>>>` to anime style."

duration.description: Video generation duration, measured in seconds, is optional. For kling-v3/kling-v3-omni: supports flexible settings of 3–15 seconds (integer); kling-o1 only supports 5 seconds; other models: enumerated values are 5 or 10. Requests that include tail frames only support 5 seconds.

video_id.description: When the action is extend, you can specify the video_id to continue the extension of that video.

cfg_scale.description: The strength of relevance of the prompt words, used to control the degree of alignment between the generated video and the prompt words, is optional. The larger the value, the stronger the association between the video and the prompt words (the creative space is smaller); the smaller the value, the higher the degree of creative freedom. The range of values is: [0, 1].

shot_type.description: Storyboard method; required when multi_shot=true. intelligence uses prompt for automatic splitting; customize uses multi_prompt.

image_list.description: Omni reference image list, only applicable to models `kling-o1` and `kling-v3-omni`. Array elements pass image links through `image_url`; optional `type` can be the first frame `first_frame` or the end frame `end_frame`. The current legacy-compatible interface accepts .jpg/.jpeg/.png, with a single image ≤10MB, both width and height ≥300px, and an aspect ratio of 1:2.5–2.5:1. A maximum of 7 images is allowed without a reference video, and a maximum of 4 images is allowed with a reference video; the end frame must be used together with the first frame. Assets must be referenced in the prompt using `<<<image_N>>>`. Omni requests do not support `negative_prompt`, `cfg_scale`, `camera_control`, or `mode=4k`.

multi_shot.description: Whether to generate a multi-shot video, only kling-v3 and kling-v3-omni are supported.

video_list.description: Omni reference video list, applicable only to the `kling-o1` and `kling-v3-omni` models, with a maximum of 1 MP4/MOV video, ≤200MB, 24–60fps. Model limits differ: the reference video for `kling-o1` is 3–10 seconds, with both width and height between 700–2160px; for `kling-v3-omni`, it is 3–15.5 seconds, with both width and height between 700–4553px, total pixels ≤8,294,400, and aspect ratio 0.4–2. `refer_type` can be `feature` or `base` (default); `keep_original_sound` can be `yes` or `no`. Materials must be referenced in the prompt using `<<<video_1>>>`. `base` cannot be used together with the first frame/last frame; when a reference video exists, `generate_audio` must be `false`. Reference videos use an independent billing tier. Base editing is billed by the actual final video duration rounded to the nearest whole second, while feature uses the requested duration; the response field usage.reference_video_seconds is the final billable number of seconds. Providing only reference images does not trigger reference video billing.

voice_list.description: Platform asset ID reference, verify ownership by user and application. Only V2.6 pro with generate_audio=true, the prompt must use <<<voice_1>>> or <<<voice_2>>>; specified voice is billed at 1.68 Credits/second.

aspect_ratio.description: Video aspect ratio, optional, enumeration values: 16:9, 9:16, 1:1. The default value is 16:9.

callback_url.description: The callback URL that will be called after the video generation is complete.

element_list.description: Platform asset ID references, ownership validated by user and application. V3, V3 Omni, and O1 only; the total number of subject and image references is limited by the model.

multi_prompt.description: 1–6 shots, with the index increasing consecutively from 1; each prompt may contain up to 512 characters; the total duration of all shots must equal the total duration. Custom shots do not use the global prompt.

end_image_url.description: End frame reference image URL. Valid only when `action=image2video` and `start_image_url` is not empty. Model/mode restrictions (consistent with Kling official documentation): `kling-v1` requires `duration=5`; `kling-v1-6`/`kling-v2-5-turbo`/`kling-v2-6` require `mode=pro`; `kling-v3`/`kling-v3-omni`/`kling-o1` support end frames in all modes; `kling-v2-master`/`kling-v2-1-master` do not support end frames.

camera_control.description: Contains 6 fields used to specify the movement or change of the camera in different directions. `camera_control.type` must be one of the following values: `simple`, `down_back`, `forward_up`, `left_turn_forward`, `right_turn_forward`. `camera_control.config` is an optional object that contains 6 optional fields: `camera_control.config.horizontal` (horizontal translation), `camera_control.config.vertical` (vertical translation), `camera_control.config.pan` (horizontal rotation), `camera_control.config.tilt` (pitch rotation), `camera_control.config.roll` (axial rotation), `camera_control.config.zoom` (zoom). The value of each field is of numeric type, with a range of [-1, 1].

generate_audio.description: Whether to generate audio while generating the video, optional. `kling-v3`, `kling-v3-omni`, and `kling-v2-6` (pro mode only) default to false. `kling-v3-turbo` comes with native audio and does not provide a switch to turn it off; omit this field or set it to true. Other models will return an error if set to true.

negative_prompt.description: Optional parameters, supporting up to 200 characters, used to describe content that you do not wish to appear in the video.

start_image_url.description: You can specify the first frame reference image of the video, which is effective when the action is image2video.
